framework_rationale: The question has two halves — what drives the decline and which actions recover 1.5 pp — so Problem → Diagnosis → Solution fits: the board must first accept that the cause is mix (not volume or freight) before the levers and the growth-policy change make sense.

candidates.text: Gross margin fell 1.9 pp because low-margin electronics grew to 19.9% of sales, not because of volume or freight; approve a 2027 plan led by electronics repricing that recovers about 1.4 pp without touching store labour, and make electronics growth margin-conditional, since the budgeted +25% would cost a further 0.7 pp.
Gross margin fell 1.9 pp on higher freight and weaker volumes; renegotiate the carrier contract and drive store traffic to recover 1.5 pp.
candidates.rejected_because: Contradicted by evidence: revenue grew 7.4% and freight sits in operating costs (H1, H3 rejected)

candidates.text: Electronics growth has diluted gross margin by 1.5 pp; the margin can be recovered with a mix of pricing and cost actions.
candidates.rejected_because: Correct diagnosis but vague on the actions and silent on the budget decision the board must take

governing_thought: Gross margin fell 1.9 pp because low-margin electronics grew to 19.9% of sales, not because of volume or freight; approve a 2027 plan led by electronics repricing that recovers about 1.4 pp without touching store labour, and make electronics growth margin-conditional, since the budgeted +25% would cost a further 0.7 pp.

key_line.message: The 1.9 pp decline is a mix problem: electronics, at 11.5% margin, grew from 13.2% to 19.9% of sales; volume grew and freight sits below gross margin
Repricing electronics, restoring grocery and apparel rates and recovering fresh and apparel sales add up to about 1.4 pp, with no store-labour cut
The plan only holds if electronics growth becomes margin-conditional: the budgeted +25% would take away a further 0.7 pp
